question: An astronaut falls straight into a black hole. Which one lets her cross the event horizon in one piece?
options: Neither would let her through intact
answer: The one of 4 million solar masses. The stretch from head to toe at the horizon falls with the square of the mass. At 10 solar masses it passes 100 g some 1,700 km outside the horizon and reaches 20 million g at it; at 4 million, it is about a ten-thousandth of a g.
move: Find where a danger peaks before assuming it peaks at the famous line.
trap: Picturing the famous stretching into spaghetti as the fate at every horizon.
reference: Thorne, The Science of Interstellar, W. W. Norton, 2014
